commits.message:
Fail and back off when the database upstream drops connections unanswered

postgres.js reconnects at once, with no backoff, when a socket closes
cleanly while a connection is being set up, and each pass restarts its
connect timeout. An upstream that accepts and closes (a proxy in front
of a dead Postgres) made the node reconnect ~700 times a second with
the pending query never settling, so the startup retry budget, the
pool-open timeout and readiness all waited silently forever. Every pool
now hands postgres.js a socket factory that turns a close before the
server's first byte into ECONNRESET: the query fails as
database_unreachable, postgres.js backs off, and the condition is
logged once when it starts and once when it clears.

Keep the TypeScript compiler out of the fault-proofs runtime barrel

The root barrel re-exported the lint-only limit-escape scanner, which
imports typescript, so the settlement worker loaded the whole compiler
under its 256 MB heap cap. Its one caller already imports it by path.
A module-graph test now refuses typescript in the barrel or the
settlement worker, and the heap probe no longer needs ESM shims.

Merge pull request #767 from Anastasia-Labs/colll78/devnet-lifecycle

Complete the devnet reliability program and merge it into the watcher checkpoint

Journal quiet recovery evidence in runs, one durable revision per run

Every finalized quiet block ran a full single-block durable authority
commit, each O(retained store), and quiet blocks never move the
finality frontier, so catching up the 2,161 blocks grown after a
correction was quadratic (over 40 minutes; the watcher journey hung
its CI shard). Quiet blocks are now observed one by one and journaled
in runs of up to 128 in one revision, before any of them is delivered.
A run stops at a touched block, the forced authority checkpoint or the
confirmation depth, and blocks waiting in a growing run are not hooked
as included. The batched authority equals block-by-block persistence.
The journey stage now takes ~3 minutes; its deadline drops to 10.

Verify the foreign commit base on idle commitment ticks

/readyz holds a node unready until its Ready history authority has
verified foreign-base evidence, but only a commit produced that
evidence, and an idle tick stops before the commit. A fresh node
before any deposit, or any node after a restart or a new history
generation, never became ready, and devnet up and the healthcheck wait
on /readyz. An idle tick now runs the commit path's own base check
against the live tail, without a lease or the worker, until the
evidence is verified.

Point the startup-retry proxy at POSTGRES_* and isolate the history authority row

The proxy forwarded to PGHOST/PGPORT, a dead port on CI where Postgres
serves 5432 through POSTGRES_PORT. The foreign DA test now clears the
singleton event_history_authority row an earlier file on the same shard
can leave behind.

Seed a verified foreign base in the readiness route fixtures

/readyz is unready until the current history authority's foreign base
is verified; the healthy-node fixtures now reach that through the real
authority and verification transitions, and one route test covers the
unverified hold.

Defer foreign adoption while a correction rewind holds on the native root

After the merge, foreign native adoption ran in the same preparation
pass as a correction rewind that had just held on the native owner's
state, replayed from a root it cannot place, and failed the history
owner. A hold on the native state now returns a marker, and adoption
waits for the next pass, as it did when such a refusal failed the pass.

Shim __filename in the settlement worker heap probe bundle

The settlement path now reaches the fault-proofs barrel, which inlines
the CommonJS TypeScript compiler; it reads __filename at load and the
ESM bundle had no such binding.

Re-pin DA bond delay, DA fixture and contract hashes to the 880 s profile

Ruling B1 moved the testing DA response windows to 880 s, which changes
the timeout and challenge validators and the compiled withdraw delay
(2,380,000 ms). The fixture is regenerated through its write channel.

Replace the synthetic native's control file atomically

The fixture's native re-reads its control file every 10 ms; a
truncate-then-write let it read an empty file, crash on JSON.parse and
end the stream under test (the CI rewind failure, ~2% under load).
Write a temp file and rename it over the control file instead.

Pass the watcher shard flag through to vitest

'pnpm test --shard' parses --shard as a pnpm option and fails. 'pnpm run test --shard' forwards it to vitest, as the fault-proof job already does.

Pin the network-id forced workflow test's size cap to its new length

The test shrank to 1,100 lines, and the module-size validator requires an exact cap.

Align two fault-proof tests with collateral release and at-tip supersession

The permissionless-slash SQLite helper still expected the collateral lease to survive confirmation. Under owner ruling G5 (fc62de472) collateral is released at confirmation, and the consumed funding stays leased until final completion. The helper now asserts exactly that.

The network-id forced workflow test expected an attempt that expired within the recovery horizon to reconcile as unknown. Under the whichever-lands-wins ruling (da234bff3) it is superseded at once, so it now reconciles as not_found with no retirement attached. The deep case still attaches retirement.

Both files pass, 11 tests.
